22.9. A page with nested headings

Date Published 01 Mar 2024

Introductory prose sitting above the page's first heading, which has no heading of its own to be addressed by.

9.1 A numbered second-level heading

Prose belonging to the second-level heading, and to nothing below it.

9.1.1 A numbered third-level heading

Prose under the third-level heading. Its ancestry runs through 9.1, and without that ancestry this passage is indistinguishable from any other paragraph about the same subject in another Part.

9.1.1.1 A numbered fourth-level heading

Prose under the fourth-level heading, four deep.

9.1.2 A sibling of the third-level heading

Prose under a heading that closes the fourth-level one above it rather than nesting inside it.

An unnumbered second-level heading

Prose under a heading the Manual did not number, which therefore has no dotted address and falls back to its position on the page.

9.3 A section long enough to be split

Paragraph one of the over-long section. Where a trade mark consists of a sign that other traders would in the ordinary course of their business and without improper motive wish to use in connection with their own goods or services, the trade mark is unlikely to be inherently adapted to distinguish, and an examiner should consider whether a ground for rejection arises on that basis alone before turning to any evidence of use that the applicant may have filed in support of the application as a whole.
